terminology.claim_protocol: The exact in-repo measurement contract for the current UPS claim: data root, task set, split, sample caps, rollout horizon, metric, promotion rule, command, ledger, and artifact bundle. A model can be fairly compared on this protocol only if it is trained and evaluated under the same contract.
terminology.external_paper_reproduction: A run of an outside paper or official implementation, or a faithful implementation with declared architecture and hyperparameters, measured on the claim protocol or on the paper's original protocol with differences explicitly mapped. Published paper table values alone are not a reproduction for this claim.
terminology.current_local_strong_baseline: The committed physical Fourier baseline is a fair neural baseline on the light-v1 claim protocol. It is not an external-paper reproduction because it uses repo-local baseline code and a local light-v1 data/compute cap.

claim_protocol.claim_scope: guarded shared-context decoded UPS candidate on held-out light-v1 test

local_strong_baseline.baseline_family: residual Fourier physical neural operator baseline
local_strong_baseline.limitation: This baseline is fair for the committed claim protocol but does not establish parity with published FNO, PDEBench, Poseidon, CNO, or other external-paper results.

external_sources.title: PDEBench official repository
external_sources.relevance: Provides official PDEBench data and baseline scripts for FNO, U-Net, and PINN.

external_sources.title: PDEBench: An Extensive Benchmark for Scientific Machine Learning
external_sources.relevance: Defines PDEBench as a benchmark suite with ready-to-use datasets and popular baseline model families.

external_sources.title: Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations
external_sources.relevance: Canonical FNO paper covering Burgers, Darcy, and Navier-Stokes style operator learning.

external_sources.title: NeuralOperator official repository
external_sources.relevance: Official PyTorch ecosystem library containing FNO and other neural-operator architectures.

external_sources.title: U-NO: U-shaped Neural Operators
external_sources.relevance: Defines the U-shaped neural operator architecture implemented by NeuralOperator UNO; useful as a second external neural-operator family after FNO.

external_sources.title: Poseidon: Efficient Foundation Models for PDEs
external_sources.relevance: Foundation-model direction with semigroup pretraining and downstream PDE evaluation.

external_sources.title: Poseidon official repository
external_sources.relevance: Official code, dataset, and pretrained-model entry point for Poseidon evaluation.

external_sources.title: PDEformer-2: A Versatile Foundation Model for Two-Dimensional Partial Differential Equations
external_sources.relevance: Equation-graph and mesh-free-query foundation-model direction; promising for symbolic conditioning, not the first reproduction path.

external_sources.title: PDEformer-2 official repository
external_sources.relevance: Official PDEformer-2 implementation and PDEBench shallow-water finetuning example.

external_sources.title: CFO: Learning Continuous-Time PDE Dynamics via Flow-Matched Neural Operators
external_sources.relevance: Cutting-edge continuous-time operator direction for long-horizon stability and irregular time grids.

external_sources.title: RealPDEBench: A Benchmark for Complex Physical Systems with Real-World Data
external_sources.relevance: Future sim-to-real benchmark gate; not comparable to the current simulated light-v1 claim.

external_sources.title: Convolutional Neural Operators for robust and accurate learning of PDEs
external_sources.relevance: Defines CNO and the representative PDE benchmark context; published table values remain unmapped to the light-v1 claim protocol.

external_sources.title: Convolutional Neural Operator official repository
external_sources.relevance: Official CNO implementation and representative PDE benchmarks; useful as a second external baseline family after FNO.

baseline_candidates.why_selected: FNO is canonical, PDEBench names it as an official baseline family, NeuralOperator provides an official implementation path, and the repo already has PDEBench-shaped data plus a local Fourier baseline for sanity checking.

protocol_mapping.comparability_note: Published PDEBench, FNO, or UNO table values are not directly comparable to light-v1 because this claim uses a capped multi-task shard, decoded rollout NRMSE, and a fixed held-out ledger. External baselines must be rerun on this protocol.

baseline_candidates.adapter_dependency_policy: optional_dependency_required_for_live_run; dry-run and contract tests are dependency-free

baseline_candidates.why_selected: UNO is a distinct NeuralOperator architecture family available in the installed external NeuralOperator package, so it broadens the claim beyond FNO without introducing a new dependency or changing the frozen light-v1 protocol.

protocol_mapping.comparability_note: Published PDEBench or FNO table values are not directly comparable to light-v1 because this claim uses a capped multi-task shard, decoded rollout NRMSE, and a fixed held-out ledger. The FNO baseline must be rerun on this protocol.

baseline_candidates.adapter_dependency_policy: optional_dependency_required_for_live_run; dry-run and contract tests are dependency-free

baseline_candidates.why_selected: PDEBench lists U-Net as an official baseline family; this adapter uses the official PDEBench U-Net architecture from commit 4ff3e3a4aa1561721b5571fa3a048a0a463e0568 and reruns it under the frozen light-v1 claim protocol.

protocol_mapping.comparability_note: Published PDEBench U-Net table values or pretrained checkpoints are not directly comparable to light-v1 because this claim uses a capped multi-task shard, decoded rollout NRMSE, and a fixed held-out ledger. This measurement reruns the attributed PDEBench U-Net architecture on the claim protocol.

baseline_candidates.adapter_dependency_policy: architecture adapted from official PDEBench U-Net source; no optional runtime dependency for dry-run or live run

baseline_candidates.why_selected: CNO is a distinct official neural-operator family with a compact MIT-licensed simplified implementation. The current light-v1 tensors are height=1 grids, so the official CNO1d path can be adapted directly under the frozen claim protocol without changing the held-out-test contract.

protocol_mapping.comparability_note: Published CNO representative-PDE-benchmark table values are not directly comparable to light-v1 because this claim uses a capped multi-task shard, decoded rollout NRMSE, flattened height=1 grids, and a fixed held-out ledger. This measurement reruns the official simplified CNO1d architecture on the claim protocol.

baseline_candidates.adapter_dependency_policy: architecture adapted from official ConvolutionalNeuralOperator simplified CNO1d source; no optional runtime dependency for dry-run or live run
baseline_candidates.adapter_scope: official CNO1d applied to the current height=1 light-v1 grids; not a CNO2d square-grid or Poseidon foundation-model evaluation

baseline_candidates.why_not_primary: Poseidon is important for the north star, but using pretrained foundation weights changes the claim from fair light-v1 baseline comparison to transfer/foundation-model evaluation. The readiness contract, adapter manifest, and validation-only ScOT checkpoint run are now recorded, but scalar light-v1 requires newly initialized embedding/recovery layers and finetuning before any held-out transfer test.

readiness_contract.required_next_step: Finetune the newly initialized scalar embedding/recovery layers on train, select on val, and only then decide whether a held-out Poseidon transfer test is justified.

baseline_candidates.why_not_primary: PDEformer-2 targets symbolic PDE conditioning and 2D problems; it is promising for architecture design but not the fastest matched reproduction against the current 1D/2D light-v1 task set.
CFO directly attacks rollout stability, but it is a newer continuous-time training recipe rather than a drop-in PDEBench/FNO baseline for the existing claim protocol.
RealPDEBench is a separate sim-to-real benchmark and should be used to prevent overbroad physics-foundation claims after the simulated PDEBench baseline path is settled.

selected_reproduction_path.required_next_step: Finetune the scalar Poseidon ScOT adapter on train and select on validation before any held-out Poseidon transfer test spend.
selected_reproduction_path.claimable_after_completion: UPS beats measured external FNO, UNO, PDEBench U-Net, and official simplified CNO1d reproductions on the same light-v1 claim protocol.
selected_reproduction_path.not_claimable_yet: UPS beats published FNO/UNO/PDEBench/Poseidon/CNO paper numbers, because published protocols, pretrained checkpoints, square-grid CNO2d setups, measured foundation-transfer protocols, and table values remain unmapped to the light-v1 claim protocol.

reproduction_contract.test_budget_rule: Use the existing held-out ledger discipline. Do not spend extra UPS candidate test budget while building the external baseline runner; only evaluate the selected external baseline once its validation behavior and schema checks pass.
comparability_rules: Use the same task set as claim_protocol.task_set.
Use train for fitting and val for adapter/hyperparameter debugging.
Use test only for the frozen reproduction measurement.
Report decoded_rollout_nrmse overall and per task.
Record command, source implementation, dependency version or commit, summary_json, artifact sha256, wall-clock time, and cost.
Do not compare against published paper table values unless every protocol difference is represented in this mapping.

foundation_transfer_contract.next_validation_gate: validation-only Poseidon ScOT adapter with pretrained checkpoint provenance, train/val-only dataset adapter manifest, decoded_rollout_nrmse on validation, and no held-out ledger write

foundation_transfer_adapter_gate.adapter_scope: Bilinear light-v1 repo field step to square Poseidon pixel_values and back to repo flattened metric shape; this measures adapter distortion, not Poseidon model accuracy.
foundation_transfer_adapter_gate.next_validation_gate: load ScOT.from_pretrained with checkpoint hash, run validation decoded_rollout_nrmse through this adapter, and only then decide whether to spend held-out transfer test budget

foundation_transfer_validation_measureme.next_validation_gate: finetune scalar embedding/recovery and any lightweight adapter on train, select by validation decoded_rollout_nrmse, and preserve held-out test until validation improves materially

comparability_decision.reason: The committed evidence proves the candidate beats a matched repo-local Fourier neural baseline, measured NeuralOperator FNO and UNO external reproductions, a measured PDEBench U-Net architecture reproduction, and a measured official simplified CNO1d reproduction on the light-v1 claim protocol. The foundation-transfer readiness contract, Poseidon adapter manifest, and validation-only Poseidon-T ScOT run are defined without held-out test use, but the Poseidon validation run is not claim-comparable because scalar light-v1 replaces the pretrained 4-channel embedding/recovery layers and still needs finetuning. The claim still does not prove superiority over published FNO/UNO/PDEBench/CNO paper table values, pretrained PDEBench checkpoints, CNO2d square-grid settings, Poseidon, PDEformer, CFO, or RealPDEBench results.
